question: According to the World Health Organization, what is the primary focus of Primary Health Care along the health continuum?

options.A: Exclusively specialized hospital treatment and advanced surgeries
options.B: Health promotion, disease prevention, treatment, rehabilitation, and palliative care
options.C: Emergency trauma care in urban tertiary medical centers

explanation: PHC focuses on a continuum ranging from health promotion and disease prevention to treatment, rehabilitation, and palliative care. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why is understanding Primary Health Care considered crucial for nursing students in Nigeria?

options.A: It shifts the healthcare focus exclusively to expensive tertiary facilities
options.B: It eliminates the need for community nurses in rural areas
options.C: It shifts the focus from hospital-centric curative medicine to community-based preventive care
options.D: It mandates that all nurses work only in private hospitals

explanation: PHC is important because it shifts the healthcare focus away from purely hospital-centric curative medicine toward community-based, preventive care. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h1)

question: In which year and location was the historic International Conference on Primary Health Care held?
explanation: The landmark International Conference on Primary Health Care took place in Alma-Ata, Kazakhstan, in 1978. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h2)

question: What primary global goal was famously associated with the Declaration of Alma-Ata in 1978?

options.A: Eradication of all known genetic disorders within a decade
options.B: Health for All by the Year 2000
options.C: Universal free university education for all health workers
options.D: Establishment of tertiary hospitals in every village

explanation: The Alma-Ata Declaration identified primary health care as the key to attaining the goal of 'Health for All by the Year 2000.' [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h2)

question: Which core principle of PHC ensures that vulnerable and marginalized populations have fair access to health services?
explanation: Equitable distribution ensures that health services are shared fairly across all population groups, especially the vulnerable and marginalized. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h3)

question: Why is intersectoral collaboration considered a vital principle of Primary Health Care?

options.A: Because health is solely dependent on hospital doctors and nurses
options.B: Because other sectors like education and agriculture heavily influence the social determinants of health
options.C: To ensure that ministries of finance control all medical prescriptions
options.D: To eliminate the need for community involvement in healthcare planning

explanation: Intersectoral collaboration acknowledges that health is influenced by many factors outside the health sector, requiring cooperation with education, agriculture, and housing. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h3)

question: Which of the following is explicitly included as an essential component of Primary Health Care?

options.D: Genomic sequencing for rare genetic mutations

explanation: Immunization against major infectious diseases is one of the core essential components outlined in Primary Health Care frameworks. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h4)

question: What is the primary significance of the essential components of PHC for community health nurses?

options.A: They serve as a guide for delivering structured, comprehensive health services at the grassroots level.
options.B: They restrict nurses from providing any form of health education.
options.C: They apply exclusively to tertiary intensive care units.
options.D: They replace the need for nursing licensure examinations.

explanation: The essential components provide nurses with a standard package of services to deliver structured and comprehensive care at the grassroots level. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h4)

question: What is a major benefit of community participation in Primary Health Care initiatives?

options.A: It ensures that health programs are culturally acceptable, sustainable, and driven by local ownership.
options.B: It shifts all financial burdens exclusively onto international donors.
options.C: It removes the need for professional healthcare personnel in rural areas.
options.D: It centralizes all medical decision-making in urban federal capitals.

explanation: Community participation ensures local ownership, making health programs more culturally acceptable and sustainable. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h5)

question: Why must the health sector collaborate with agriculture and education to address childhood malnutrition?

options.C: Because health workers are not allowed to talk about food
options.A: Because food production and nutritional education fall under external sectors that impact overall health determinants
options.B: To increase the cost of medical consultations
options.D: To eliminate the need for primary health clinics

explanation: Intersectoral collaboration is necessary because agriculture and education directly influence food supply and nutritional knowledge, which are key health determinants. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h5)

question: Which agency is responsible for coordinating Primary Health Care at the national level in Nigeria?

options.A: Federal Ministry of Works and Housing
options.B: National Primary Health Care Development Agency (NPHCDA)
options.D: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria

explanation: The National Primary Health Care Development Agency (NPHCDA) is charged with coordinating PHC policies and development nationally in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h6)

question: What is a common structural challenge affecting Primary Health Care centers in rural areas of Nigeria?

options.A: An overwhelming surplus of specialized neurosurgeons
options.B: Shortages of skilled personnel, poor infrastructure, and essential drug supply issues
options.C: Excessive funding leading to institutional inflation
options.D: Too many operational ambulances per clinic

explanation: Rural PHCs in Nigeria frequently struggle with poor infrastructure, a shortage of skilled workers, and unreliable essential drug supplies. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h6)

question: What is a major financial barrier that prevents low-income families from accessing care at primary health facilities in Nigeria?

options.A: Free universal medical services for everyone
options.B: High out-of-pocket spending for healthcare services and drugs
options.C: Mandatory state-funded health insurance coverage for all citizens

explanation: High out-of-pocket spending forces families to pay directly for care, creating a major financial barrier and risking impoverishment. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h7)

question: How can task-shifting and task-sharing policies help mitigate workforce shortages in Nigerian Primary Health Care centers?

options.A: By allowing trained nurses and community health workers to safely deliver certain expanded lifesaving services
options.B: By restricting healthcare delivery exclusively to foreign specialist physicians
options.C: By shutting down primary health clinics to reduce staffing needs
options.D: By eliminating all clinical training requirements for nursing students

explanation: Task-shifting and task-sharing optimize the available workforce by empowering trained nurses and community health workers to provide expanded essential care. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h7)
